page: Microsoft Azure M128bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor operating at frequencies up to 4.0 GHz. The instance provisions 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 64 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 105 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 1024 GB of system memory, establishing a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are not present, and the instance provides no local disk storage, requiring external network-attached block volumes such as Azure Premium Storage for persistent file systems.

Performance benchmarks show top-tier throughput in parallel compute and memory subsystems. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 433.45 GB/sec, while write operations achieve 185.13 GB/sec, supporting heavy data-shuffling operations. The instance attains a PassMark CPU score of 106668.0 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 110229.0. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression registers at 647.83 GB/sec. Specialized vector extensions including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) allow CPU-based machine learning inference, delivering 36.99 tokens per second for prompt processing on 70B parameter models.

System tradeoffs center on the balance between single-thread execution and aggregated parallel density. Single-core benchmark metrics position the CPU in the middle-to-upper percentiles, confirming that workload efficiency relies on multi-threaded parallelization rather than individual thread speeds. The reliance on remote storage also necessitates consideration of network storage throughput limits for disk-bound tasks. The M128bs_v3 is well suited for enterprise in-memory databases like SAP HANA or Redis, large-scale data analytics, caching clusters, and high-concurrency transactional database engines.
description: Microsoft Azure M128bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for high-density enterprise workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C x86_64 processor reaching 4.0 GHz, the instance supplies 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores and 1024 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. No discrete GPU or local storage is included, directing data persistence to network-attached block storage. Benchmark metrics confirm exceptional multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth, reaching 433.45 GB/sec in large block uncached reads and 185.13 GB/sec in writes. Real-world key-value tests reflect this architectural strength with 138.25 million Redis SET operations per second alongside top-tier database operation scores. While single-thread benchmarks remain moderate, advanced instruction support including AVX-512 and AMX delivers capable matrix math and CPU-based inference. The M128bs_v3 is strategically matched for enterprise in-memory databases, large caching layers, data engineering workloads, and large-scale transactional enterprise systems.
